Immich is a self-hosted photo and video backup solution.

For immich, there are multiple helm deployments:

  • immich-web
  • immich-server
  • immich-typesense
  • immich-machine-learning
  • immich-microservices (this one)

For redis and postgres, there are multiple helm charts:

  • Redis: app-template/redis, bitnami/redis
  • PostgreSQL: operator cloudnative-pg/cloudnative-pg, bitnami bitnami/postgresql

#!/bin/bash

set -o errexit
set -o nounset

curl --silent --location https://github.com/DavidMoore/ipfilter/releases/download/lists/ipfilter.dat.gz --output /tmp/ipfilter.dat.gz
gunzip /tmp/ipfilter.dat.gz
result=$(kubectl get pod --selector app.kubernetes.io/name=qbittorrent --output custom-columns=:metadata.name --namespace default)
QBITTORRENT_POD=$(echo $result | awk '{ print $NF }')
if [[ $QBITTORRENT_POD == *"qbittorrent"* ]]; then
  kubectl cp /tmp/ipfilter.dat default/$QBITTORRENT_POD:/config/ipfilter.dat
  kubectl rollout restart deployment qbittorrent --namespace default
else
  echo "qbittorrent deployment not found"
  exit 1
fi

METRICS_URL="http://localhost:9374/metrics"
HEALTHY_FILE="/tmp/smokeping-healthy"
prev_responses=""
gateway_was_down="false"
touch "$HEALTHY_FILE"
while true; do
  sleep 30
  requests=$(wget -qO- "$METRICS_URL" 2>/dev/null \
    | grep 'smokeping_requests_total{host="10.0.7.1"' \
    | awk '{print $2}')
  responses=$(wget -qO- "$METRICS_URL" 2>/dev/null \
    | grep 'smokeping_response_duration_seconds_count{host="10.0.7.1"' \
    | awk '{print $2}')
  # If we can't scrape metrics at all, stay healthy (avoid restart loop)
  if [ -z "$requests" ] || [ -z "$responses" ]; then
    touch "$HEALTHY_FILE"
    prev_responses=""
    gateway_was_down="false"
    continue
  fi
  # Detect gateway down: requests incrementing but responses frozen
  # (or responses equal requests means no loss, so down = responses frozen
  # while requests are ahead).
  # Simpler signal: if responses haven't changed since last check and
  # requests != responses, the gateway is not responding.
  if [ -n "$prev_responses" ] && [ "$responses" = "$prev_responses" ] && [ "$requests" != "$responses" ]; then
    gateway_was_down="true"
    touch "$HEALTHY_FILE"
  elif [ "$gateway_was_down" = "true" ] && [ -n "$prev_responses" ] && [ "$responses" != "$prev_responses" ]; then
    # Gateway was down and responses are now incrementing again —
    # trigger a restart to recycle all raw ICMP sockets.
    rm -f "$HEALTHY_FILE"
    gateway_was_down="false"
  else
    touch "$HEALTHY_FILE"
  fi
  prev_responses="$responses"
done

targets:
  # Local gateway - used as health signal by the sidecar healthcheck
  - hosts:
      - 10.0.7.1             # OPNsense gateway
    interval: 1s
    network: ip4
    protocol: icmp
    size: 56
  
  # Public DNS Servers (IPv4)
  - hosts:
      - 1.1.1.1              # Cloudflare Primary
      - 1.0.0.1              # Cloudflare Secondary
      - 8.8.8.8              # Google Primary
      - 9.9.9.9              # Quad9 Primary
      # 149.112.112.112 is used for WAN2 gateway monitoring in OPNsense
    interval: 1s
    network: ip4
    protocol: icmp
    size: 56
  
  # Internet Services
  - hosts:
      - google.com
      - github.com
      - cnn.com
      - ghcr.io
    interval: 1s
    network: ip4
    protocol: icmp
    size: 56

conditions: ["len([BODY]) == 0"]
group: internal
dns:
  query-name: "{{ .Release.Name }}.unscfleet.com"
  query-type: A
url: 1.1.1.1
